same explicit review as changing the block.

**Rationale.** Hardware does not retain Rust lifetimes. Once a pointer is
copied into a TSS, IDT, DMA descriptor or similar table, validating it at the
store is insufficient; the mapping must be non-revocable for at least the
hardware lifetime. A distinct token makes that stronger fact visible at the
only setter, while the address-space record makes it true after the token is
dropped.

Per-file fingerprints are intentionally coarser than per-block hashes. The
sound-wrapper rule is about every safe path surrounding an unsafe operation,
and a narrow block hash would miss a removed bound or widened public
constructor elsewhere in the same file. Eighteen reviewed records are a small
cost for making such drift a gate failure.

**Alternatives.** Re-walking `IST1` before a double fault is impossible: the
processor selects the stack before ordinary handler code runs. Consuming a
`MappedStack` at the setter would remove one Rust value but would not stop a
separate safe `unmap` call. Leaking the frames without recording the virtual
extent would keep physical memory allocated while still allowing the live PTE
to disappear. A `Drop`-based syscall transition was rejected because safe
`mem::forget` can skip `Drop`; a closed function leaves no obligation behind.
Per-block fingerprints and the former textual counter were rejected because
both omit relevant safe-wrapper changes.

**Consequences.** Release and debug QEMU now report 212/212, including `the
double-fault stack cannot be unmapped`. The first inline-`Slot` implementation
made the already-deep debug settlement path overflow its guard; the full gate
caught it, and moving the singleton record beside `ACTIVE_ROOT` restored the
unchanged `AddressSpace` layout before this decision landed. Removing the
active-root refusal let an inactive
space mint a token; removing the overlap refusal unmapped the live IST stack;
both produced exactly that one failed check. Changing strict half-open overlap
to include an adjacent guard edge failed only its host arithmetic test.
Zeroing the syntactic span accumulator failed only the unsafe-counter fixture,
and making the raw MMIO constructor safe failed only the reviewed-fingerprint
test. All five transformations were restored and persist, bringing the
mutation registry to 200.

The semantic pass found no further current defect in the instruction/register,
descriptor/trap/context, page/frame/heap, boot-ABI, port/MMIO, user-copy,
extended-state or synchronization families. PW-401 remains the explicit
VERIFY row for the shared-page compiler and future SMP memory-order contract;
this UP audit does not pretend to close it. PW-703 remains trigger-only as
described above. The unsafe allowance did not grow: it remains 368 measured
lines against 380.

## D-215 Operational Markdown is checked; historical numbers stay historical — Status: Accepted (2026-08-28), amends D-146; closes PW-507

**Context.** D-146 corrected thirteen numeric claims but explicitly stopped
before `008` through `012`. Later prose checks tied two current Phase 6 totals
to source, while every local Markdown path, heading fragment and written
`cargo xtask` invocation remained unchecked. A moved document could leave a
plausible blue link to nowhere, and a renamed task could remain the command a
reader was told to run.

The deferred numeric pass found one actual contradiction. D-76's unsafe
boundary checkpoint had 75 machine checks. D-77 then added four during the
completed-phase audit and states that Phase 4 closed at 79, which is also the
baseline `011` uses. The closing paragraph in `009` nevertheless called the
75-check intermediate point the phase close. The same pass found a prospective
`gdb` xtask formatted as a concrete executable command even though no such task
exists.

**Decision.** The host prose suite now reads every project-authored Markdown
document under `docs/` plus the root, userland and repository-tool guides. A
local link must remain inside the workspace and name an existing path. A
fragment must name a generated heading anchor in the target document. Upstream
bootloader documentation is not rewritten or made part of this project's
promise.

Every `cargo xtask` invocation formatted as inline code or a fenced command is
fed to the same CLI parser that runs the tool. A bare `cargo xtask` remains
legal prose because the docs deliberately use it to describe the error case;
a proposed task is named as a proposal rather than formatted as an executable
command.

`014`'s closing table remains the one current numeric summary. Its machine
count is derived from `EXPECTED_CHECKS`, its mutation total from the registry,
its later-individual count must equal total minus the last full sweep, and its
last decision must equal the decision log's last heading. `016` points to that
checked table instead of copying the changing machine and mutation totals into
three more current-facing cells.

**2026-09-06 enforcement correction.** A later paragraph in `014` still called
the image “current” beside an obsolete 189-check total, even though the closing
table had advanced. The prose check now rejects a current numeric restatement
outside that table while continuing to permit explicitly dated and
“then-current” historical evidence. The same pass makes contributor and README
guidance name both PW-601 prerequisites and the separate VMware transcript
qualification step. Six focused defects remain mutations 1,343 through 1,348.

The manual `008`–`012` pass preserves measurements made at their dated
research and slice checkpoints. Each document now says explicitly that
numbers, tool versions and words such as “current” are scoped to that date;
later correction notes and this log govern the present tree. `009` now
distinguishes D-76's 75-check checkpoint from D-77's 79-check phase close.
This is the distinction D-146 required: correcting a false historical claim
without replacing valid history with today's unrelated total.

**Rationale.** Local target existence, heading identity and CLI grammar are
cheap, deterministic properties with repository-owned sources of truth. They
belong in the ordinary host suite. External URL availability does not: a
network-dependent gate would turn a remote outage into a source failure and
would still not prove that the cited page supports the sentence.

Current counts need one checked restatement, not a growing collection of
copies. Historical measurements need a date and an honest correction, not a
rewrite that makes an old decision appear to have observed future work.

**Alternatives.** A general Markdown package was unnecessary for the current
inline-link and generated-heading surface; the deliberately small reader has
fixtures at the exact forms the repository uses. Pinging every external URL
was rejected as nondeterministic and semantically weak. Replacing all old
totals with 212 was rejected because it would falsify phase evidence rather
than repair it. Maintaining another hand-written list of xtask names was
rejected because the real parser is already the authority.

**Consequences.** Pointing README's architecture link at a missing file and
pointing AGENTS' Development link at a missing heading each failed only
`every_local_markdown_link_and_anchor_resolves`. Renaming the documented
`test-boot` task failed only `every_documented_xtask_invocation_parses`.
Changing `014`'s current machine total failed only
`the_phase_close_says_what_the_source_says`. All four transformations were
restored and persist, bringing the mutation registry to 204. External-source
truth and prose semantics remain reading work; this decision closes the
structural and numeric gap, not the wider reproducibility work in PW-508 and
PW-509.

## D-216 Release evidence binds clean source and resolved inputs to reproducible, booted bytes — Status: Accepted (2026-08-28), closes PW-508

**Context.** The local gate proved ten ordered properties, image construction
read the kernel back from its filesystem, and D-25 pinned vendored binaries.
Those were separate facts. No one record said which clean source tree, Cargo
lock, compiler, emulator, firmware, storage namespace, kernel and disk image
participated in one passing qualification. Rebuilding in the ordinary target
directory also reused enough state that two successes were not evidence of
reproducibility.

An evidence file committed beside the source cannot name its own commit and
hash without a self-reference loop. A timestamped report would change when
nothing relevant did. A successful gate transcript would still not establish
that the image whose hash it prints is the image the shipped-kernel runner
booted.

**Decision.** `cargo xtask evidence` starts and ends with the same clean Git
commit and tree and refuses modified or untracked source. Kernel builds now
always pass `--locked`. The task snapshots `Cargo.lock`, `rust-toolchain.toml`,
Rust and Cargo versions, the resolved QEMU executable and version, both UEFI
firmware inputs, every vendor listing and payload, and the deterministic NVMe
namespace. Every QEMU runner uses that same resolved installation. The NVMe
builder now compares complete content rather than reusing any file of the
expected length.

After the typed local gate passes, the task removes only four fixed children
under `target/evidence/`, builds the shipped release in two fresh private Cargo
target directories, and requires the kernel ELFs and disk images to agree in
both length and SHA-256. It copies both pairs into the bundle, boots the exact
path-A copy, requires the liveness challenge and settlement, and hashes that
copy again after QEMU exits. Only then does it write `wizard-evidence-v1`.

The manifest is a sorted, timestamp-free key/value record under ignored build
output. It carries source and input identities, the fixed relative artifact
paths, lengths and hashes, every gate-stage result, the artifact-identity
result and the exact-artifact boot result. `cargo xtask verify-evidence` does
no build and contacts no network. It rejects malformed, duplicate, missing or
unknown fields, requires every result to be `pass`, re-resolves and rehashes
the current clean source and installed inputs, re-verifies vendor completeness,
and independently hashes all four bundled artifacts.

**Rationale.** The manifest is useful only if the authorities it joins are the
ones execution used. One QEMU resolver prevents the recorder and runners from
quietly naming different firmware. Two erased target directories distinguish
reproduction from an incremental rebuild. Booting the bundled copy, then
rehashing it, closes the last gap between “an image was produced,” “these bytes
were recorded,” and “a shipped kernel was exercised.”

Keeping the bundle outside Git avoids the commit/hash loop and keeps two
64 MiB disk images out of source history. Omitting time and absolute paths
makes identical inputs render identical evidence. The commit and tree retain
the historical identity; a later checkout can verify the bundle only when it
matches that identity.

**Alternatives.** Building twice in one Cargo target was rejected because it
mostly proves cache reuse. Recording only logs was rejected because prose does
not bind an artifact. Committing the manifest was rejected because it either
lies about its source commit or requires an unending sequence of successor
commits. A container or virtual-machine image for every host tool is wider
than this row and would still need firmware and hypervisor policy; PW-509 owns
the remaining pin-versus-record decisions. Signing was rejected because the
project has no release key or external verifier whose trust decision would
make a signature meaningful.

**Consequences.** On clean commit `b88e752`, the complete gate passed with
1,472 compiler-resolved API items, 188 host unit tests (one ignored helper),
and 212/212 machine checks in both release and debug. Independent target paths
produced identical 3,462,408-byte kernel ELFs at
`082e09c7b00a43318896abe01bc66921de2ebcc8c3575d9adbd9a3062628945f`
and identical 67,108,864-byte disk images at
`4daa81dd59618330843dbdafe4b7154d3ab0d807e19af8181fc6eb136b2221dc`.
The exact bundled path-A image booted, took the injected keyboard interrupt,
settled and retained that digest. A separate offline verifier invocation
accepted the manifest and bytes.

Removing lock enforcement, accepting a same-sized foreign namespace,
accepting duplicate or inexact schema fields, equating artifacts by size,
accepting a failed result, accepting dirty source, changing field order, or
trusting a recorded artifact digest each failed only its exact host check. All
nine transformations were restored and persist, bringing the mutation
registry to 213. This record covers the self-contained local gate and shipped
QEMU artifact; it does not turn the deliberately separate VMware, TLC or full
mutation qualifications into CI, and it does not close PW-509's remaining
environment recreation policy.

## D-217 Process birth and death evidence names one exact incarnation — Status: Accepted (2026-08-29), pairing evidence removed by D-248; closes PW-515

**Context.** The clean evidence refresh after D-216 exposed an intermittent
debug failure in `a spawned program holds exactly one handle`. The check made
the child runnable, then read its live bootstrap table, ring and address space.
The emitted program is deliberately short: a timer interrupt could run it
through exit before the observer reached any of those reads. The same check,
and three neighbouring ring-program checks, then treated any increase in a
global retirement count as this child's death and read the last record for a
reusable slot. Neither half named the process whose facts it claimed.

A first repair carried the birth snapshot through `Spawned` and captured it
inside the by-value commit. That was logically exact but increased the nested
debug stack enough to drive the already-large process transaction into its
guard page. Two boots double-faulted at `Option<AddressSpace>::take`, at
different later spawns. A detached build of unchanged `5ca4227` passed all
212 checks; restoring the original `spawn_transaction` and commit frame sizes
made the repaired kernel pass too. Evidence code may not perturb the boundary
it is meant to observe.

**Decision.** Self-test builds record an immutable `Birth` immediately before
the reserved thread commits and becomes runnable. It contains the authority
table's non-repeating identity, initial live-handle count and bootstrap kind,
the kernel-owned ring shape and the ring mapping's flags. `Spawned` carries
that table identity, and `birth_of` returns a record only when the slot and
identity both match. D-248 removed the former parent-end/peer comparison after
the production caller audit showed the paired endpoint existed only to satisfy
this check.

The birth record lives in a fixed per-slot side table rather than in the
transaction's return value. Recording is a separate call that returns before
the original by-value commit begins, keeping the debug transaction and commit
frames at their clean-tree sizes. A returned `Spawned` can have a birth record
only after every resource has been prepared, and the thread remains
`Reserved` until the immediately following commit succeeds.

`LastRites` now carries the same non-repeating table identity. Every check that
reads a program's ring exit record waits for that identity, not for a global
retirement count and not for whichever program last occupied the slot. The
racy live-table and live-ring helpers are gone. The global counter remains for
checks whose independent trap/fault record already identifies their event.

**Rationale.** A table identity already has the no-reuse property this proof
needs (D-204); inventing a second process generation would duplicate a harder
invariant. Capturing prepared objects while scheduling still says `Reserved`
turns a timing observation into a construction fact. Keeping birth evidence
and last rites keyed by the same identity makes “born with one” and “died with
one” statements about one incarnation even after its numeric thread slot is
reused.

**Alternatives.** Sleeping or lengthening the probe program only widens the
race. Clearing stale rites on spawn prevents one false positive but does not
identify a later overwrite or stabilize the birth observation. Teaching the
program a test-only wait protocol would add target ABI behaviour solely for a
kernel check. Enlarging `Spawned` or the commit frame was rejected by the
measured debug stack faults.

**Consequences.** The original repaired debug boot passed 212/212. D-248 later
removed the pairing-only state and replaced its retained break with corruption
of the returned table identity; the same check must then reject the mismatched
incarnation. Removing the obsolete live-table helper also required retargeting
D-126's existing leaf-lock mutation to the production authority lookup; its
property and registry cardinality are unchanged. The failed D-216 evidence
refresh was not release evidence and was regenerated by later qualification.

## D-218 Qualification names a stable machine and every resolved tool — Status: Accepted (2026-08-29), closes PW-509

**Context.** D-216 bound a clean source tree to verbose Rust/Cargo/QEMU
versions, the QEMU executable, both firmware files, every vendored input and
the exact booted bytes. It still passed `-machine q35`, whose meaning changes
when QEMU advances: on the current installation it resolves to
`pc-q35-11.1`. The exceptional phase-close paths were outside the record too.
`model-check` invoked whichever `java` happened to be on `PATH` without naming
it, while `vmware` printed a bare `vmrun` command even on the current machine,
where Workstation is installed at its standard Windows location but is not on
`PATH`.

**Decision.** Every QEMU runner uses the explicit `pc-q35-9.2` machine type.
The stable hardware shape is pinned in source; the evidence record continues
to bind the QEMU executable and firmware bytes which implement it. Rust stays
pinned by `rust-toolchain.toml`, with the resolved compiler and Cargo verbose
identities recorded alongside that file's digest and `Cargo.lock`.

Evidence format v2 adds fixed-shape identities for Java and VMware's `vmrun`:
availability, normalized version output, executable length and SHA-256 are
present whether or not the optional tool exists. Absence is the literal value
`unavailable`, not a missing field. The verifier compares availability before
the remaining bytes, so a host lacking a tool used by the recorded
qualification names that dependency and both states exactly. Changed versions
or executables name their exact differing field.

One resolver owns each exceptional path. TLC prints Java's full identity and
executes that resolved path. VMware generation probes only `vmrun`, never the
GUI or a VM; it prints the CLI's identity and fully quoted path when present,
and otherwise produces the portable VM directory with an explicit unavailable
diagnostic. Version probes have a five-second deadline and reap a timed-out
child, so environment discovery cannot become an unbounded qualification job.

**Rationale.** A versioned QEMU machine is the one stable input in this set;
recording what an alias meant after a run would document drift rather than
prevent it. Java and VMware cannot reasonably be vendored into this Rust
workspace, but a fixed record makes their absence and substitution
machine-checkable without making them prerequisites for ordinary CI or local
release evidence. Recording the executable as well as its self-reported
version catches repackaged bytes carrying the same display string.

**Alternatives.** Keeping `q35` and relying on the QEMU digest was rejected
because the same source would silently request a new hardware ABI after a tool
upgrade. Requiring Java and VMware for `ci` or every evidence build was rejected
for D-18/D-26's existing reason: missing exceptional tools must not teach a
contributor to skip the local gate. Vendoring a JVM or a VMware appliance would
greatly widen the repository and still not license or reproduce the host
hypervisor. Absolute installation paths were rejected because they identify a
directory layout, not tool bytes, and make an otherwise portable manifest
host-specific.

**Consequences.** The resolved Java path ran TLC 2026.08.21 with Microsoft
OpenJDK 21.0.5: 2,901 states generated, 1,040 distinct, depth 49 and zero
errors. VMware generation identified `vmrun version 1.17.0 build-24583834`,
printed its usable absolute command and started no VM. Replacing the versioned
machine with `q35`, retaining `vmrun` usage text as its identity, changing an
unavailable tool's schema and skipping the availability-first comparison each
failed only its named host witness. All four transformations were restored and
persist, bringing the mutation registry to 218. A committed format-v2 evidence
bundle and QEMU boot still have to be regenerated before this successor commit
is called qualified; the exceptional results above prove tool resolution, not
the phase-close PW-001 through PW-004 evidence on a final commit.

## D-219 Limine remains the boot boundary; current prose names current facts — Status: Accepted (2026-08-29), amends D-03 and closes PW-514

**Context.** The post-audit register named a small but misleading residue in
current-facing prose. Phase 5's close still presented closure-under-leaf-guard
and stale `MappedStack` defects as live after D-121 and D-125 closed them, did
not name D-189's later closure of the broad active-space door, called the
per-CPU lock count global after D-154, paired D-164's implemented timed wait
with the still-uncalled wait on multiple queues, and could be read as claiming
dynamic stacks or a first-class `MemoryObject`. The Phase 4 close still called
timed waits and both guarded stacks open; the boot and research notes called a
shipped initrd and D-162's anchored backslash code future or unresolved. The
I/O-port module still warned that i8042 chained two permanent claims even
though D-138 made that pair atomic.

One contradiction required a decision rather than editing. D-03 and the
roadmap retained an own-bootloader Phase 12 side quest, while the later
foundation audit explicitly declined it: Limine is maintained, vendored and
digest-pinned, and writing the same UEFI handoff again has no unmet kernel or
Wizzy caller.

**Decision.** Historical phase proposals, dated counts and observed results
stay historical and are labelled as such where a nearby current summary could
confuse them. Current-facing summaries name the decisions which superseded
their old debt and distinguish infrastructure which actually exists from the
triggered first-class abstractions which do not.

The project keeps Limine as its boot boundary. An own bootloader is not roadmap
work and is not a standing side quest. Reconsideration needs a concrete defect
in the required handoff which the maintained dependency cannot satisfy; the
mere opportunity to rewrite it is not a trigger.

**Rationale.** An ADR and a phase narrative serve different purposes. The ADR
must preserve what was decided and why; a current summary must not make a
reader reconstruct every later amendment before learning what exists. Adding
"historical" to genuine evidence preserves it. Repeating a closed defect as a
live one does not.

Limine already supplies the versioned handoff, has exact vendored provenance
and participates in release evidence. Replacing it would consume a complete
platform project while advancing neither kernel correctness nor the closed
Wizzy compiler gate. That violates D-183/D-184's finite-work rule unless an
actual unsupported requirement appears.

**Alternatives.** Silently removing the Phase 12 item was rejected because it
would contradict D-03 without recording why. Keeping it as an optional
side quest was rejected because roadmap entries are invitations even when
called optional. Rewriting historical phase evidence to present-day totals or
capabilities was rejected because it would invent evidence the old run did not
produce.

**Consequences.** D-03 and the current roadmap point here; the boot contract
states that module loading now carries the initrd. The Phase 4 and Phase 5
closes distinguish paid debts, absent caller-driven abstractions and genuinely
open work. The i8042 comment describes the atomic pair it now uses. A prose
host check pins these current claims while separately requiring the dated
Phase 5 check and unsafe-line totals to remain explicitly historical. The one
measured `redundant_clone` in the ACPI test is removed without adopting the
noisy nursery lint group. Targeting that lint with `deny`, all-graph Clippy,
rustdoc and the complete host suite passed; the suite contained 193 passing
tests and one intentionally ignored interruption child. Restoring the retired
own-bootloader roadmap failed only
`current_facing_foundation_prose_names_the_later_resolutions`; the restored
transformation persists as mutation 219. The full reviewed port abstraction
still contains 16 unsafe blocks and 10 unsafe declarations, and its new exact
source fingerprint records the prose-only review.

## D-220 The dependency record is offline; advisory freshness is exceptional — Status: Accepted (2026-08-29), amends D-16, D-25 and D-26; closes PW-510

**Context.** The locked Rust graph had grown to 67 registry packages, three of
which reach the shipped kernel, while the repository also carried three
checksum-pinned third-party or generated artifacts. `Cargo.lock` names exact
crate bytes but no license. Cargo metadata names the crate license but misses
the SIL Open Font License on the Noto glyph data embedded by the MIT-licensed
font crate. No machine-readable SBOM said which inputs ship, and no policy said
whether a clean checkout, an already hydrated checkout or an advisory database
was meant by “self-contained.” The local machine does not have `cargo-audit`;
making that absence fail every build would contradict D-26 rather than improve
the dependency record.

**Decision.** `supply-chain/inventory.txt` is the reviewed source of dependency
and license conclusions. Every registry tuple is bound to the name, version
and checksum in `Cargo.lock`; every vendored artifact is bound to its checked
path and SHA-256. Each row says whether it reaches the runtime image or only
development, and license conclusions include non-code data such as the Noto
glyphs. A repository-owned parser, SPDX 2.3 renderer and digest checker use no
registry cache, package manager, network or new dependency. The committed
`foundation.spdx` must be byte-for-byte what that inventory renders.

The network boundary has two explicit stages. A first checkout may run
`cargo fetch --locked` to hydrate the exact locked crate archives and rustup
may install the pinned toolchain and target, as D-16 already allowed. After
that, the complete gate must pass with Cargo offline; the supply-chain check
itself works even before hydration because it reads only committed bytes.

Vulnerability freshness cannot be made offline and current at once. At every
phase close and before a public release, a deliberately exceptional RustSec
`cargo audit` run examines `Cargo.lock`; its tool version, advisory-database
revision, time and result belong in the qualification record. It is not in
ordinary `ci`, and absence is reported as absence rather than presented as a
green advisory result. A distributable image is accompanied by the generated
SBOM, the project license and third-party notices; a bare disk image is a build
artifact, not a complete distribution bundle.

**Rationale.** Checksums, license conclusions and shipped scope are review
facts, so they belong beside the source and must remain verifiable when the
network and Cargo cache are absent. Advisory status is a time-varying external
fact, so committing a once-fresh database or silently accepting a stale one
would confuse reproducibility with currency. The split preserves both: local
CI proves exactly what was reviewed, while qualification records when the
external claim was actually refreshed.

**Alternatives.** Adding `cargo-deny`, an SPDX crate or an online service to
the ordinary gate was rejected because the checker would add the dependency
it is meant to inventory or make D-16 depend on a host install. Treating
`Cargo.lock` as an SBOM was rejected because it lacks licenses, shipped scope,
vendored inputs and the font-data license. Calling a fresh checkout offline
without first fetching locked archives was rejected as an impossible promise.
Vendoring the entire crate registry and advisory database was disproportionate
for one developer and would turn timely external data into a large stale tree.

**Consequences.** The checked inventory names 67 registry packages and all
three vendored artifacts; its manifest-derived kernel closure identifies the
three linked crates plus `BOOTX64.EFI` as the four runtime inputs. The
deterministic SPDX 2.3 document, runtime copyright notices and complete
OFL-1.1 text are committed distribution paperwork. The complete 11-stage gate
passed after dependency hydration with Cargo forced offline: xtask's 200 tests
passed, one interruption child remained intentionally ignored, and every
library test and doctest passed. Release and debug QEMU each passed 212/212
machine checks before the shipped and degraded images settled.

Changing a locked dependency checksum, runtime scope, selected license,
vendored digest, notice identifier or committed SPDX bytes each failed only
its named host witness. Allowing an ambiguous dependency name to select one of
two locked versions failed its resolver witness. All seven restored
transformations persist as mutations 220 through 226. The phase-close
checklist gains one exceptional advisory result; it does not gain a
permanently installed tool or an ordinary CI stage which can fail only because
the network is unavailable.

## D-221 A queue index is the synchronization edge, not a volatile payload — Status: Accepted (2026-08-29), amends D-79, D-84, D-112, D-113 and D-115; closes PW-401

**Context.** D-79 required `READ_ONCE()`-shaped access, D-113 copied each
shared entry once, and the Phase 5 implementation put a spin lock around the
kernel's `Shared` handle. None of those facts ordered ring 3. `Shared::read_at`
and `write_at` forwarded to ordinary `copy_nonoverlapping`; the compiler could
merge, move or elide accesses to memory an external agent changes. The lock
serialized kernel callers only. The current one-CPU trap route and x86 store
ordering hid the gap, while an SMP kernel or compiled runtime would have had
no stated happens-before edge between an entry and the index publishing it.

D-84 had proposed a Shuttle test which weakened `Release`/`Acquire`. D-112
records the measured result: it passed because Shuttle explores schedules
under sequential consistency, not weak-memory visibility. Keeping that test as
the proof would repeat the exact false oracle already found in Phase 5.

**Decision.** Each queue direction is SPSC and has one fixed four-step
contract. The producer volatile-writes a complete entry and any associated
data, then release-stores its naturally aligned 32-bit tail. The consumer
acquire-loads that tail before volatile-copying the entry exactly once, and
release-stores its head only after it is finished with the copy. The producer
acquire-loads the head before reusing the slot. Counters remain little-endian
free-running `u32`s; their existing wrapping validation remains separate from
memory ordering.

The index access itself is atomic. Volatile prevents invention, merging and
elision of payload accesses but supplies no ordering; a fence around an
ordinary or volatile index is not a substitute for an atomic index which
synchronizes with its peer. `wost::mm::Shared` therefore exposes bounded,
aligned `load_acquire_u32` and `store_release_u32` operations with no caller-
selected ordering, plus volatile byte-copy operations. Its former ordinary
shared-copy methods are gone. `kernel::queue` can express only the four
protocol edges through those named methods. Pages and private protocol state
share one bounded lock, making concurrent kernel completion paths one logical
producer; a second CPU cannot advance and publish tail 2 before the first has
written slot 0. The time page also moves onto the volatile payload boundary,
while retaining its distinct sequence-counter fences.

The hand-emitted x86-64 client has no compiler and uses naturally aligned
`mov`s, which implement acquire loads and release stores under x86 TSO. It now
acquires `completion_tail` before reading the completion and releases
`completion_head` after validation, in addition to releasing its submission
tail. The future compiled Wizzy runtime must express the same operations with
its platform atomics and volatile accessors; application code never selects an
order or touches the layout.

**Proof.** A four-event host model enumerates every order of payload
visibility, index visibility, index read and payload read. Observing a new
index with an old payload requires `index-visible < index-read` and
`payload-read < payload-visible`. Release adds `payload-visible <
index-visible`; acquire adds `index-read < payload-read`; together the four
constraints form an impossible cycle. Weakening either edge admits a concrete
order. The check reads the actual `wost` method bodies and the queue helpers,
so it is not a detached model of a protocol the implementation need not use.
A separate source check forbids the ordinary-copy bypass and pins both volatile
operations. The generated-client check pins payload, SQ release, CQ acquire,
completion reads and CQ release in execution order.

**Alternatives.** Treating the trap or spin lock as the barrier was rejected
because userspace does not take it and another CPU need not enter the same
critical section. Volatile indices were rejected because volatile is an
access property, not inter-thread ordering. `SeqCst` everywhere would be
correct but would erase the ownership-specific protocol and impose stronger
portable instructions than the proof needs. Making every entry field atomic
would still allow mixed-version records and obscure the copy-once validation
boundary; publication protects the volatile record as a unit. A probabilistic
stress test or x86 disassembly alone cannot prove the weak-memory property, and
Shuttle has already demonstrated that it cannot model it.

**Consequences.** The shared-memory wrapper grows two reviewed unsafe lines
and remains inside its 380-line budget at 370. Five checks were each broken
against their exact defect: release and acquire were independently weakened to
`Relaxed`, the volatile store became ordinary, and the real client acquired
its own head instead of the completion tail; splitting completion state from
page publication recreated the two-producer hole. Each failed only its named
host witness; the restored transformations persist as mutations 227 through 231.
The full gate and ring-3 boot result are recorded in PW-401's closing row.

## D-222 A foreign handle has the same answer whether its slot is occupied or absent — Status: Accepted (2026-08-29), amends D-78 and D-95; closes PW-403

**Context.** D-78 made one global arena safe through a final table-owner
comparison, but gave that comparison its own `NotYours` result while empty and
reused slots returned `Stale`. D-95 made the distinction load-bearing in a
check so deleting the ownership comparison could no longer pass unnoticed.
That proved authority did not cross, but it also preserved the oracle later
named by D-115: given the correct table mixer and an exact slot-generation
candidate, the two errors revealed whether another table still occupied it.

The maximum architectural result leak was one bit per exact candidate:
`NotYours` meant a matching live foreign entry, while `Stale` meant no matching
entry. Repeating probes could inventory candidates but reveal no object or
authority. The shipped ring already collapsed every resolution error to
`STATUS_BAD_HANDLE`; leaving the distinction in the kernel API would let a
future direct Wizzy handle operation accidentally freeze it into a new ABI.

**Decision.** `HandleError::NotYours` is removed. Resolve and close still
compare the full non-repeating table identity, but an owner mismatch returns
`Stale`, exactly as an empty or reused slot does. `Malformed` remains distinct:
it describes the caller's value rather than arena state. The mixer remains a
deterministic accident barrier rather than a secret or an authority check.

This closes the architectural result oracle, not every timing side channel.
Handle lookup is not promised constant-time, and no authorization property
depends on occupancy being secret. The stable interface guarantee is the one
the implementation can prove: live-foreign and absent probes return the same
error and neither changes either table.

**Proof.** The real-arena machine experiment inserts an object in one table,
encodes its exact slot and generation with a second table's mixer, and applies
both resolve and close. It then closes the owner's handle and repeats both
operations against the now-absent candidate. All four observations are
`Stale`; the foreign attempts leave the owner and both counts unchanged.
Deleting the resolve ownership comparison makes the live probe succeed;
deleting the close comparison removes the other table's entry. Each defect
reddens only `a handle reveals no foreign occupancy`.

**Alternatives.** Keeping the distinction because today's ring flattens it was
rejected because the pre-Wizzy foundation exists to settle precisely these
future seams before a caller freezes them. Replacing the global arena with one
allocation per table would remove shared occupancy but discard D-78's bounded
commitment and scaling shape for an error distinction no caller needs. A
secret mixer would require an entropy policy Phase 8 owns and would still not
replace the owner comparison.

**Consequences.** The machine-check count stays 212 because D-95's cross-table
check is strengthened rather than duplicated. Both ownership paths were
broken independently and restored; mutations 232 and 233 retain them. The
full release/debug result is recorded in PW-403's closing row.

## D-223 CPU-local guards and syscall wakes have durable direct witnesses — Status: Accepted (2026-08-29), amends D-68 and D-133; closes PW-405

**Context.** Two compiler and machine facts had each been checked only once.
D-68 manually observed `E0277` after making lock guards `!Send`, but `wost`
cannot run doctests and copying a guard-shaped stand-in into `libs/` would
only test the copy. D-133 fixed trap-context wakeups after finding that a
`RingEnter` completion could make a kernel waiter Ready without arming the
tickless timer, but its lasting check drove the keyboard proxy. The exact
syscall experiment was constructible and remained unbuilt.

**Decision.** A host compile-fail harness creates a temporary `no_std` crate
which path-depends on this checkout's actual `wost`, asks a generic `T: Send`
function to accept `SpinLockGuard` and `ThreadLockGuard` separately, and
cross-checks each offline for the compiler's `E0277`. No production type or
auto-trait mechanism is copied. `SpinLockGuard` no longer repeats a marker:
its owned `InterruptState` is the CPU-local proof and the thread-lock guard
keeps its direct marker.

The machine harness uses the real user process and ring. A self-test-only gate
stops one child in ordinary kernel thread context before its first user
instruction. A kernel waiter registers on that child's `Queue::waiters`, and
the harness observes both registrations before releasing the child. Its Echo
submission and `RingEnter` trap then call the production `Queue::serve` →
`WaitQueue::wake_all` → `thread::unblock` path. A cancellation condition exists
only so failed setup cannot strand a test thread.

`RingEnter` samples D-133's production handler-arm counter immediately around
`serve`. That narrow observation is necessary: the child's following Exit
trap wakes the mandatory reap worker and legitimately increments the global
counter a second time. Waiting for the ring waiter to run is not substituted
for observing the arm; an already-armed slice can run it on the broken kernel.

The spawn and observation phases are separate functions. The first debug boot
put the observation frame beneath `spawn_transaction`'s deliberately large
unoptimised frame and reached the boot stack's guard while committing the
`AddressSpace`; keeping that frame out of the spawn call restored headroom
without enlarging every kernel stack. The debug gate then passed the exact
path that exposed the harness error.

**Proof.** The restored release machine boot observed both waits registered,
one exact RingEnter arm, the waiter returned, Echo completed and answered its
own token, the child exited without a user fault, and both thread slots were
returned. Reinstating D-133's trap exemption preserved every consequence but
left the RingEnter arm at zero; only `a syscall wake arms the timer for what it
woke` failed, at 211/212.

Changing `InterruptState`'s marker to `PhantomData<()>` made the actual
`SpinLockGuard` satisfy `Send`; changing the thread guard's marker did the same
there. Each made `contracts::guard_types_do_not_cross_cpus` fail because its
expected compiler refusal became a successful compile. Both changes persist
as mutations 234 and 235; D-133's existing mutation now names the direct
syscall witness.

**Alternatives.** A source grep for `PhantomData` was rejected because it
would bless spelling rather than the auto trait. A stand-in `libs/` type was
rejected because it could drift while the production guard became `Send`.
Keeping the keyboard proxy was rejected because the caller that exposed the
defect now exists and can be orchestrated without a race. A delay before
`RingEnter` was rejected because timing is not registration evidence.

**Consequences.** The machine-check count remains 212: the direct syscall
check replaces D-133's proxy. The mutation registry grows to 235. The guard
contract adds no Cargo feature graph and no shipped code; its temporary crate
is compiled only by the host test. PW-405 is closed.

## D-224 The boot memory map is complete or refused — Status: Accepted (2026-08-29); closes PW-108

**Context.** The boot handoff copied at most 128 physical-memory regions into
a fixed array and counted every later entry as dropped. Logging that loss did
not restore the evidence: the allocator selected usable frames, the direct map
selected memory, and firmware/device checks excluded ranges using only the
accepted prefix. Even where omission merely lost RAM on today's ordered maps,
the type still claimed to be the bootloader's memory map while proving less.

This copy runs before the heap exists. Dynamic storage would introduce a
dependency cycle, raising the constant would move rather than resolve the
boundary, and adjacent-region coalescing cannot bound an alternating valid map.

**Decision.** `libs/memory-map` owns the safe, allocation-free region types
and policy. Its constructor consumes the complete input stream, accepts one
through 128 regions, and returns a typed `Empty` or `TooMany { reported,
capacity }` error without exposing a copied prefix. The Limine adapter only
translates protocol kinds and maps that error into `HandoffError`; it no
longer pushes entries one by one. `wost::mm::Report` consequently has no
`dropped_regions` state because no initialized allocator can have one.

The fixed capacity remains 128. Refusal is deliberate degradation: the kernel
can report the handoff error while staying on the bootloader's mappings, but it
does not initialize its allocator or replace the page tables from incomplete
ownership evidence.

**Proof.** Host maps at 127 and 128 entries round-tripped every region in
order. At the exact bound, useful, firmware and reserved tail entries changed
the allocatable total, first direct-mapped run, complete coverage and
memory-only coverage independently. A 129-entry input returned `TooMany` with
both exact counts and no `MemoryMap` value. Replacing the overflow mark with
the former `continue` accepted the first 128 as an `Ok` map and reddened only
`tests::the_region_limit_is_all_or_nothing`; mutation 236 retains that defect.

**Alternatives.** Heap allocation was rejected because the map is what creates
the heap. A larger fixed array was rejected because every finite silent cap has
the same defect. Checked coalescing was rejected as the sole answer because it
cannot reduce alternating kinds and risks erasing boundaries whose kind is the
policy input; it could be added before the same refusal only if measured boot
maps ever require it.

**Consequences.** Memory-map policy becomes ordinary host-tested Rust and
`wost::boot` re-exports it, preserving callers while shrinking the unsafe-file
review surface. The machine-check count remains 212; the mutation registry is
236. PW-108 is closed.

## D-225 A retained PIT qualifies and can revoke public time — Status: Accepted (2026-08-29), amends D-36, D-57, D-152, D-166, D-181 and D-201; closes PW-303

**Context.** Boot measured the timestamp counter and local-APIC timer against
two agreeing PIT windows, then parked the PIT for the rest of the boot. The
invariant-TSC bit was diagnostic only. VMware had already produced one
unexplained calibration refusal, while a rate change or stalled TSC after a
successful boot had no observer and the time page's `MODE_NONE` was only a
manually exercised protocol. A post-launch failure could therefore publish
wrong time, strand an admitted Timer, or leave a program without D-201's
preemption guarantee.

The available CPUID frequency leaves are not interchangeable. Leaf 0x15 gives
a TSC-to-crystal ratio only when denominator, numerator and crystal frequency
are all nonzero. Leaf 0x16 reports a nominal core MHz value, not necessarily
the TSC rate. Hypervisors may omit either leaf or describe a virtual frequency
which is less persuasive than a successful measurement against an independent
device.

**Decision.** PIT measurement remains the preferred boot source. When its TSC
windows refuse, a complete leaf 0x15 ratio may supply the TSC rate only if the
processor also advertises an invariant TSC; two bounded APIC windows must then
agree against that rate. Leaf 0x16 is retained for diagnostics only. The PIT
is parked on final refusal but otherwise remains claimed by the clock.

Every scheduler appointment is capped at forty milliseconds, within one
unambiguous PIT span. Arming the APIC starts a PIT window and records the TSC;
the APIC expiry samples both. A window is stable when the PIT is near the
planned expiry and its derived TSC rate is within one sixty-fourth of the boot
rate. An early APIC expiry or a TSC disagreement is conclusive. A late or
possibly folded window is inconclusive because host descheduling and slow
hardware are indistinguishable after delivery. A delivered older interrupt is
also inconclusive when the newly armed APIC counter remains nonzero; otherwise
it could accuse the replacement timer from a window only microseconds old.
Stable or inconclusive evidence breaks the failure streak; two consecutive
conclusive disagreements revoke the public clock. One was rejected after QEMU
produced a single false revocation during the first implementation boot.

Revocation records the last trusted nanosecond, freezes `now_ns`, makes the
live-calibration predicate false and publishes `MODE_NONE`. The desired mode
is stored independently of the page owner so revocation cannot be lost while
`install` temporarily moves that owner out to allocate page tables. Sleeping
threads are made runnable, their queues settle Timer operations exactly once
with `STATUS_UNAVAILABLE` when serviced, and future Timer and process admission
is refused. Kernel sleeps stop re-parking when trust is lost.

Public time and scheduling progress deliberately separate at that point. Each
later APIC delivery advances a private scheduler epoch by the simultaneous PIT
sample. The scheduler continues one-shot preemption and accounting against that
epoch without exposing it through Uptime or the time page. Idle still means no
appointment and no housekeeping tick. This validator is sampled by APIC
delivery: it detects an early APIC and a drifting or stopped TSC when an expiry
arrives, but cannot discover an APIC which never interrupts. Adding an
independently routed interrupt or NMI watchdog is a different hardware policy,
not a property inferred here.

Suspend and resume remain unsupported. There is no attempt to reconstruct an
elapsed interval across power-state discontinuity; a machine which adds that
path must requalify or replace the source before it can resume public time.

**Proof.** Host tests keep the exact leaf 0x15 ratio distinct from leaf 0x16's
nominal MHz, reject every incomplete or zero-rate answer, and distinguish
stable, stopped, early, stale-delivery and latency-ambiguous watchdog windows.
Release QEMU
injects two stopped-TSC decisions through the production streak, observes a
nondecreasing frozen public clock, a progressing private scheduler epoch,
`MODE_NONE`, and one admitted Timer's exact unavailable terminal completion;
the test then restores the live state for the remaining machine suite. The
existing page-revocation check removes the page owner while publishing
`MODE_NONE` and observes the deferred mode after restoration.

Exchanging the CPUID numerator and denominator, comparing the observed TSC
rate with itself, letting an older interrupt judge the new timer, requiring a
third disagreement, dropping the deferred page mode and suppressing private
scheduler progress each reddened only its named host or machine witness. All
six defects persist as mutations 237 through 242. The release and debug
machine suites pass 213 checks.

**Alternatives.** Promoting leaf 0x16 to a clock rate was rejected because it
names a different quantity. Preferring CPUID over a successful PIT measurement
was rejected because measured virtual hardware is the stronger local fact.
Continuing to publish the TSC after disagreement was rejected because a mode
which cannot revoke is not a trust gate. Stopping all alarms on revocation was
rejected because it recreates D-201's unpreemptible-program defect. A periodic
PIT interrupt was rejected because it would add routing and a permanent tick;
HPET or ACPI PM-timer support remains justified only by a machine which needs
it. Panicking on the first disagreement was rejected after the real QEMU false
positive demonstrated the cost.

**Consequences.** Long appointments use forty-millisecond validation steps;
the two-hundred-millisecond sleep witness therefore expects five useful
expiries rather than one. The page's conversion remains immutable, while its
permission is now a live production state. The machine-check count is 213 and
the mutation registry is 242. PW-301 and PW-003 still own the current VMware
observation; this decision does not upgrade QEMU's CPUID or APIC evidence into
one.

## D-226 The Wizzy handoff is an exact route-neutral envelope — Status: Accepted (2026-08-29), closes PW-600

**Context.** D-183 requires a versioned standalone artifact and separable
runtime before product integration. `015` already said the artifact format,
target, platform ABI, runtime and effect encoding must agree, and that the OS
must consume pinned bytes rather than a neighbouring checkout. Those facts
had no single machine-readable record. Adding loader or runner code now would
freeze the delivery-route guesses PW-601 explicitly stops; leaving only prose
would make the first real integration invent its version and provenance rules
under schedule pressure.

**Decision.** `libs/wizzy-handoff` owns an allocation-free parser for the
`wizard-wizzy-handoff-v1` envelope. A record carries, in one canonical ordered
key/value form:

- the `x86_64-unknown-wizard` target and `wizard-platform-v1` aggregate
  platform ABI;
- exact artifact, runtime and effect-encoding version tokens;
- a sorted, duplicate-free set of effect requirements;
- one HTTPS repository and exact lowercase Git identities for source,
  compiler and runtime, plus a SHA-256 dependency-lock identity; and
- the artifact's canonical decimal length and lowercase SHA-256 digest.

The OS-owned target and platform identifiers are fixed constants. The three
Wizzy-owned version tokens are not guessed here: the verifier accepts only the
exact values its integration caller supplies. Unknown format versions, fields
and mismatched target or ABI values are refusals. Effect names are metadata
returned to launch policy; accepting the record never mints a handle or
authority.

There is intentionally no artifact kind, runner, load address, path or
delivery-route field. The envelope identifies and authenticates opaque bytes;
WZ-002 and WZ-003 still own what those bytes mean and which runtime consumes
them. Adding or changing a field requires a new envelope version rather than
teaching an old reader to guess.

`handoff/conformance-v1.wzh` is a committed conformance fixture beside an
opaque payload. Its artifact/runtime/effect tokens use the reserved `fixture.`
namespace and its provenance identities are syntactic fixture pins, so it
makes no claim that a Wizzy artifact exists. An `xtask` repository test hashes
the adjacent payload and passes the result plus explicit expected versions to
the pure parser. Neither parsing nor the fixture consults the network,
environment or a sibling checkout.

**Proof.** Host tests accept the committed fixture only with the SHA-256 of
the adjacent bytes and require platform v1 to remain entry, ring and time-page
v1. They refuse an unknown envelope, an unknown, duplicate or reordered
field, non-canonical values, every target and ABI mismatch, and an identity
where only length or digest agrees. Changing the supported envelope constant,
bypassing the header or extra-field guards, accepting malformed values,
accepting every version, weakening identity to either length or digest,
changing the fixture bytes, or changing the time-page version each reddened
its exact host witness. All eight defects persist as mutations 243 through
250.

**Rationale.** Exact caller-supplied tokens let the future image build pin the
compiler-owned sides of the seam without this repository claiming to know
them early. One aggregate platform version lets a producer reject the native
entry/ring/time contract as a whole; their existing internal version fields
remain the finer wire checks. Canonical ordering, spellings and encodings make
the record byte-stable and reviewable. Recording both length and digest avoids
treating a hash string as the identity of bytes no consumer actually read.

**Alternatives.** Choosing bytecode, ELF or Wasm in the record was rejected
because the readiness evidence does not support that decision. Reading
`../wizards-ink` was rejected because it would make ordinary CI depend on
ambient state. Hard-coding speculative Wizzy artifact/runtime versions was
rejected because those versions belong to WZ-002 and WZ-003. A permissive
TOML/JSON document was rejected for this small contract because ignored or
duplicated fields and multiple equivalent serializations are exactly what a
version envelope must exclude.

**Consequences.** The OS side can now validate a complete identity envelope
and pinned bytes before any consumer exists. Gate opening must supply real,
reachable provenance and explicit supported version tokens in this format;
the conformance fixture cannot satisfy WZ-001 through WZ-004. A future need
for multiple repositories, another digest, or new metadata is an envelope-v2
decision, not an optional v1 field. PW-601 remains stopped until the real
artifact and runtime seam exist. The mutation registry is 250; no machine
check was added.

## D-227 QEMU runs own their writable state and every control endpoint — Status: Accepted (2026-08-29), closes PW-512

**Context.** QMP already avoided a bind/connect race by making `xtask` listen
before QEMU dialled it, but the human monitor did not. Its port was found by
binding port zero, reading the result, dropping the socket and asking QEMU to
bind the same number later. Another local process could take that port in the
gap. Every run also copied the firmware variable template to the same
`target/efi-vars.fd`; two otherwise independent runners could therefore write
one firmware store. The first two-run experiment exposed the same defect in
the boot artifact itself: both builders truncated `target/wizard-os.img`, and
one failed while reading back a short `wizard-kernel.elf`. A first construction
of the shared NVMe corpus had no cross-process exclusion either. Finally,
every disk path was interpolated into QEMU's comma-separated `-drive`
key/value syntax without escaping commas. `Command` preserved spaces as one
argument, but that did not make the argument's inner grammar safe.

**Decision.** Each boot reserves both QMP and human-monitor loopback listeners
before spawning QEMU. QEMU is the client for both; the exact human-monitor
suffix is `server=off`, because a real boot proved that QEMU rejects `wait` in
client mode. The harness accepts and keeps one monitor stream, consumes its
initial prompt once and uses the same bounded connection for every later
query. No control port is ever probed, dropped and rebound.

Each run creates a unique variable-store file with `create_new` beneath the
fixed `target/qemu runs,private/` directory, copies the pristine firmware into
that already-owned file and removes it on drop. The process ID plus a
monotonic in-process sequence makes names diagnostic; `create_new`, not the
name, establishes exclusivity. A QEMU consumer likewise reserves its own boot
image with `create_new` in that directory and removes it on drop; the explicit
`cargo xtask image` artifact remains the canonical `target/wizard-os.img`.
The NVMe corpus moves beneath `target/qemu storage,private/`, so every gate
boot exercises a real path containing both a space and comma. An OS advisory
lock serializes its read/repair/write transaction with a five-second bound.

All file-valued `-drive` arguments go through one encoder which doubles commas
for QEMU's key/value grammar. Spaces remain ordinary bytes in the same
`OsString`; no shell is involved. Device-option commas are still syntax and
are not escaped. Shared boot and NVMe bytes use QEMU's private snapshot mode:
the emulated device may write, but those writes cannot alter another run's
base. The QMP injector also receives the run deadline and a cancellation flag
and is joined on every exit path. A harness-requested stop waits for QEMU to be
reaped before private-file guards drop, so Windows has released the handles
when cleanup runs.

**Rationale.** Holding a kernel socket is the only local proof that its port
is reserved. Retrying a guessed port merely narrows the race. Writable UEFI
state and a boot under construction belong to one virtual machine, not shared
build output. A read-only NVMe backend was rejected by the real QEMU
controller, so a temporary snapshot is the isolation primitive it can consume.
Exercising the hostile directory names in every real boot proves the path
encoder against the same QEMU parser and bytes the gate relies on, while a pure
argument test identifies the exact doubling rule when a boot fails before
storage comes up.

**Alternatives.** Fixed ports were rejected because they make concurrent runs
mutually exclusive. Unix sockets were rejected as the only route because the
host gate is Windows. Letting QEMU remain the monitor server with a retry loop
was rejected because it still cannot reserve the chosen port across process
launch. Quoting the whole `-drive` value was rejected because `Command` does
not invoke a shell and quotes would become literal QEMU input; the comma is
inside QEMU's grammar and must be escaped there.

**Consequences.** Concurrent runners have disjoint control sockets, firmware
stores, boot images and guest-write overlays; shared NVMe construction is
serialized and a completed corpus is reused only after its complete contents
match. Two simultaneous shipped boot checks both built, booted, advanced their
keyboard IRQ count from 24 to 30 and settled; the failed precursor is what
found the shared-image race. Release self-test QEMU passed 213/213 through the
real comma/space paths, and the shipped check exercised repeated commands on
one accepted monitor stream. Reaping before teardown left the private-run
directory empty. Eight deliberately broken host witnesses went red and persist
as mutations 251 through 258. No machine check was added.

## D-228 Extended-state proof follows every enabled component — Status: Accepted (2026-08-29), advances PW-305 to VERIFY

**Context.** The eager switch saves the `XCR0` mask x87 + SSE + AVX, but its
only restored-value witness wrote the low quadword of `xmm0`. That observes SSE
inside the legacy area. It says nothing about the x87 stack beside it or AVX's
upper halves in component 2, so either component could be omitted while the
check and D-108's claim remained green. D-144's sentinel proves the selected
form stays inside its buffer; it deliberately does not prove the form wrote
everything it claims.

**Decision.** One narrow `xstate::Probe` is the complete machine witness for
the mask this kernel permits. It carries an exactly representable x87 integer,
the low quadword of `xmm0`, and the high quadword of `ymm0`. Its write pushes
the x87 value, writes the SSE lane and inserts the AVX lane; its read extracts
the lanes and pops the x87 value. The same two-thread switch experiment gives
both threads three different values and requires all three to return intact.
The x87 write resets that stack before pushing: the first break attempt merely
pushed both threads' values, and their LIFO execution order made an omitted
x87 save look correct. With the reset, each write replaces the live witness
instead of leaving the other thread's value underneath it. The wrappers refuse
unless extended state is live and all three component bits are enabled. They
remain the only target code which uses floating-point/vector instructions,
under the existing `+soft-float,-sse` contract.

One named operation mask feeds both save forms and restore. Persistent
mutations clear x87, SSE and AVX from that mask independently, so each claimed
component must make the same machine check red. The existing mutation which
skips the complete save/restore path remains the fourth witness.

**Form coverage.** The ordinary QEMU `-cpu max` boot executes standard
`XSAVE`; the current TCG explicitly warns that it cannot provide an opt-in
`XSAVEC` bit. A current VMware self-test must therefore execute the same
three-component check through production `XSAVEC`. Historical compacted boot
evidence predates this witness and is not credited to it. PW-305 becomes
`VERIFY`, owned by PW-003's current VMware round rather than by a fake CPUID
configuration.

**Alternatives.** Inspecting saved bytes was rejected because x87/SSE legacy
encoding and compacted AVX placement would make the check another parser of
the implementation. Checking three registers without a switch was rejected
because it proves only that the probe instructions agree with themselves.
Enabling AVX-512, AMX or another component solely to test it was rejected:
every enabled bit costs per-thread memory and D-82 admits only components with
a caller. Forcing `+xsavec` under TCG was rejected after the emulator reported
that it cannot implement the requested feature.

**Consequences.** Release QEMU passed all 213 checks through standard `XSAVE`.
Clearing x87, SSE or AVX independently then reddened only `every enabled state
component survives a switch`, each at 212/213; mutations 259 through 261 retain
those exact defects. The initial push-only x87 witness staying green under its
omission is itself the D-28 result which required the reset. The compacted half
remains one specific hardware observation, not open-ended implementation work;
once the current VMware image passes the same named check, PW-305 is `DONE`.
No state beyond the already enabled mask is added. The reviewed target wrapper
adds ten lines to the unsafe audit surface, now exactly 380 against its
unchanged 380-line ceiling, and advances only `xstate.rs`'s pinned fingerprint.

**Current disposition (2026-08-31).** The implementation finding is resolved,
so PW-305 is now `REQUIRED` rather than `VERIFY`: only PW-003's fresh
compacted-`XSAVEC` VMware observation remains.

## D-229 The ring model carries visibility through every terminal owner — Status: Accepted (2026-08-29), closes PW-404

**Context.** D-112's TLA+ model proves admission accounting over anonymous
counts. D-221's four-event host litmus proves that one release tail and one
acquire read exclude a published index beside an old payload. Neither proof
carries that visibility edge through the operation whose reservation may end
normally, by cancellation or during process retirement. Shuttle cannot fill
the gap: its scheduler is sequentially consistent, which D-112 already proved
by watching a deliberately Relaxed model stay green.

**Decision.** `models/RingMemory.tla` is the finite, identity-bearing model for
that composition. Two distinct operations each reuse one message state first
for a submission and then for its completion. Payload issue, payload
visibility, tail issue, tail visibility, tail acquisition and payload read are
separate transitions. Release permits tail visibility only after payload
visibility; acquire permits the payload read only after the tail observation.
The same transitions therefore cover both queue directions rather than
crediting a one-way publication proof twice.

Admission occurs only after the submitted payload was acquired and takes its
reservation in the same transition which makes the operation live. Normal
completion, cancellation and retirement are three distinct settling causes.
All retain the live identity until terminal publication; that transition
spends exactly its reservation, records one report and changes the same message
state to completion publication. Reaping happens only after the completion
payload is acquired. The checked invariants require no stale payload read,
one reservation per live operation, bounded completion ownership, at most one
terminal report per identity, no vanished admitted operation and explicit
reachability of all three causes.

The correct configuration is not trusted by itself. Four adjacent mutant
configurations independently remove release ordering, acquire ordering,
reservation at admission or the one-shot terminal guard. `cargo xtask
model-check` requires the correct model to finish clean and requires every
mutant to violate its exact named invariant; a mutant that becomes clean or
fails for another reason is a failed qualification. Cancellation and
retirement each have a distinct model state and are required reachable, so
TLC cannot collapse their transitions into the normal path.

The model is also bound back to source at the ordinary host gate. The existing
D-221 checks pin the real atomic and volatile publication operations. New
source checks require `Queue::take` to reserve before consuming or publishing
the submission head, require the settling flag to be claimed under its one
lock, require terminal publication before a pending slot is removed, and
require cancellation and retirement to use that same settlement path. Real
production mutations remove reservation and the one-shot settling guard; the
older release/acquire mutations remain the source-side reordered-memory
witnesses.

**Alternatives.** Enlarging `Ring.tla` was rejected because its anonymous
counts are the clearest proof of admission capacity, while message visibility
and terminal identity would obscure that small model and multiply its state
space. Another Shuttle test was rejected by the measured false green above.
A stress test on x86 was rejected because TSO cannot exhibit every ordering a
portable Wizzy runtime must express. A prose mapping from the model to source
was rejected because it can drift while both code and model remain green.

**Consequences.** Microsoft OpenJDK 21.0.5 and TLC 2026.08.21.155922 completed
the original accounting model at 2,901 generated / 1,040 distinct states and
depth 49, then completed the new model at 2,809 generated / 1,296 distinct
states and depth 31. The four relaxed-store, relaxed-load, no-reservation and
duplicate-terminal configurations violated `NoStalePayload`, `NoStalePayload`,
`ReservationsAreLive` and `OneCompletionPerOperation` respectively. The task
rejects a mutant which becomes clean or names a different invariant.

Removing the real reservation increment, the real one-shot settling guard and
retirement from the model's reachable actions each reddened only its new
source/model-bound host check before restoration; they persist as mutations
262 through 264. D-221's release/acquire mutations 227 and 228 remain the
production memory-order breaks. The model check stays an exceptional Java
qualification, while model inventory, complete invariant registration, exact
mutant registration, cause reachability and both source bindings run in every
CI. A missing checker now points to its actual vendoring instructions, with
that recovery path pinned by mutation 265. No target code, wire ABI, unsafe
operation or machine check changed.

## D-230 Foundation performance is a repeatable observation, not an ABI promise — Status: Accepted (2026-08-29), closes PW-511

**Context.** The foundation had correctness gates but no stable answer to a
correctness-preserving change which doubled the kernel image, consumed a new
class of retained memory or made a boundary path orders of magnitude slower.
`010-research-notes-3.md` also records the essential limit: QEMU/TCG time is
not bare-metal performance evidence. Treating one emulator duration as a
product promise would manufacture precision, while recording nothing leaves
the cheapest large regressions invisible.

**Decision.** `cargo xtask baseline` is a bounded qualification task over the
pinned QEMU machine, not a CI stage and not a benchmark of hardware. It builds
the self-test image once per debug and release profile and boots each image
three times. Every boot must retain the ordinary complete self-test verdict.
The task reports every sample, the observed range and a versioned, separately
reviewed threshold band for each profile; those bands are regression alarms,
not ABI or throughput guarantees.

Host measurement owns facts the guest cannot improve by reporting them:
kernel ELF bytes, fixed disk-image bytes and the syntactic unsafe-line count.
The self-test kernel emits one strict `baseline v1` record after all checks. It
records calibrated time from clock origin to the start of self-test, free
frames, all three heap counters, committed and occupied handle-arena slots,
the TSC rate, one ring-3 `int 0x80` Echo round trip and one maximum-buffered
4 KiB NVMe read. The round trip brackets the actual user instruction on both
sides with fenced timestamp reads and leaves its delta in an otherwise unused
submission field after the kernel has consumed the request. It is therefore a
measurement of the boundary and its minimal real queue service, the path a
Wizzy runtime will call, rather than a kernel function timed from inside
itself. Storage brackets a real polled DMA command and converts ticks with the
same calibrated rate the kernel publishes.

The two dynamic witnesses are also ordinary machine checks: zero ticks, a
faulting child, a missing completion or a read which did not fill the whole
buffer is a correctness failure before it is a performance sample. The host
parser refuses duplicate records, missing or reordered fields, unknown
versions, arithmetic overflow and a baseline attached to anything but a clean
verdict. Pure tick conversion and band/variance evaluation stay in `xtask`,
where host tests cover their boundaries. Each new check gets its deliberate
red witness and persistent mutation.

**Alternatives.** Host wall-clock time was rejected because scheduler load can
move it without changing one guest instruction. `-icount` as a universal
answer was rejected because it changes the virtual timer model whose real
calibration, sleeps and I/O this image is meant to exercise; instruction count
can become an additional baseline later without replacing these paths. A
single run was rejected because it cannot state variance. Putting six more
boots in CI was rejected because the bands are descriptive qualification and
the ordinary debug/release boots already gate correctness. Timing only kernel
functions was rejected because it bypasses the ring-3 and device boundaries
whose regression matters to the future Wizzy caller.

**Consequences.** The tightened task passed all six 215-check boots. Release
observed 5,109,630 to 5,378,776 ns to self-test, 114,885 free frames, heap
state 20/1,002/4, empty handle state, 24,552 to 26,982 ns at the trap boundary
and 26,869,503 to 33,474,843 bytes/s from storage. Debug observed 26,835,732 to
29,484,274 ns, 114,265 to 114,266 frames, heap 20/1,002/4, empty handles,
105,937 to 201,668 ns and 7,479,097 to 8,701,422 bytes/s. Both profiles read
exactly 4,096 bytes. Their kernel ELFs were 6,725,512 and 8,648,304 bytes;
both images remained exactly 67,108,864 bytes; `wost` remained 380 unsafe
lines in 170 blocks.

The reviewed release bands are 6.4 to 7.1 MB ELF, 3.5 to 9 ms boot, 114,800
to 115,000 free frames, 16 to 24 slab / 990 to 1,010 large / exactly 4 live
heap allocations, empty handles, 10 to 100 microseconds at the ring boundary
and 10 to 100 MiB/s storage. Debug uses 8.2 to 9.1 MB, 20 to 45 ms, 114,150
to 114,400 frames, 14 to 24 / 990 to 1,010 / exactly 4 heap state, empty
handles, 50 to 400 microseconds and 3 to 20 MiB/s. Both require a 3 to 4 GHz
calibrated counter, the exact 64 MiB image, exact 4 KiB read and the existing
exact unsafe count.

The exploratory first debug repetition also found the self-test coordinator
had no headroom to retain another resource snapshot: `Option<AddressSpace>`
needed an 872-byte debug frame and crossed the guarded boot stack. Baseline
state now lives outside that coordinator frame; one direct debug boot and both
subsequent three-run qualifications passed the formerly faulting path. The two
production breaks each reddened only their named machine check at 214/215;
strict-record, two-sided-band, documented-command and emitted-selector breaks
each reddened only their exact host test. Mutations 266 through 271 retain
those defects. No unsafe operation or wire ABI changed. No threshold is a
compatibility promise, and a threshold change is a reviewed measurement update
rather than an ABI decision.

## D-231 A debugger owns one paused machine and discovers its endpoint — Status: Accepted (2026-08-29), closes PW-513

**Context.** The kernel has retained DWARF and QEMU has a GDB stub, but the
documented Windows workflow still stops at a raw `-s -S` suggestion. That
leaves debugger selection, symbol loading, the remote endpoint and cleanup to
every investigation. A fixed TCP port conflicts with concurrent runners, and
probing a free port before QEMU binds it repeats the race D-227 removed from
the other machine controls. Rust's `rust-lldb` launcher is installed here but
no LLDB executable is; the native WinLibs package does provide GDB 17.2.

**Decision.** The supported route is the exact native GDB identity shipped by
WinLibs POSIX/UCRT `16.1.0-14.0.0-r4`: `GNU gdb (GDB for MinGW-W64 x86_64,
built by Brecht Sanders, r4) 17.2`. `GDB` may name its executable explicitly;
otherwise the task searches `PATH` and the WinGet package directory. A changed
identity is refused until it is reviewed rather than silently becoming the
debugger baseline.

`cargo xtask debug` builds the unoptimised shipped kernel, starts one headless
QEMU machine paused at reset and opens GDB with that ELF's symbols. The run
owns a private boot image and firmware-variable store, snapshots every shared
disk and always terminates and reaps QEMU when GDB exits. QEMU dials an HMP
listener the harness already owns. HMP starts the GDB server on loopback port
zero and `info chardev` reports the assigned address; no fixed port or
probe/rebind interval exists. The initial command uses a hardware breakpoint
at the linker entry `kmain`, continues to it and leaves the interactive prompt
there.

`cargo xtask debug --check` is the non-interactive acceptance path. It has a
fixed deadline, requires GDB to hit `kmain`, emit an exact marker and produce a
symbolized frame naming `wizard_kernel::kmain` at `wost/src/boot/mod.rs`, then
detaches. Success, refusal and timeout all converge on the same QEMU cleanup.
The debugger remains an exceptional developer dependency and does not enter
CI; the host gate checks its command construction, endpoint parsing, pinned
identity and proof-output parser without requiring GDB.

**Alternatives.** LLDB was rejected for the present setup because a Cargo
wrapper without the debugger it launches is not a tool. WSL or
`gdb-multiarch` was rejected because D-16's build is native Windows and a
second environment buys nothing now that native GDB reads the kernel ELF.
QEMU's conventional port 1234 and a guessed free port were rejected because
both make otherwise independent runners contend. Leaving QEMU alive after a
debugger failure was rejected because an overnight or automated proof must not
strand a paused machine.

**Consequences.** The bounded command resolved the exact WinGet GDB, opened a
dynamic loopback endpoint, hit `wizard_kernel::kmain` at
`wost/src/boot/mod.rs:526`, emitted its marker and symbolized frame zero, then
detached and reaped QEMU in 3.3 seconds. The interactive command reached the
same source line and `quit` also removed its private image and variable store;
neither path left a GDB or QEMU process.

Accepting port zero, an unreviewed GDB identity, a software breakpoint before
the higher-half entry was mapped and a backtrace missing either its symbol or
source each reddened only its exact host check before restoration. Renaming the
documented task reddened only the existing prose/CLI check. Mutations 272
through 276 retain all five defects. No target code, unsafe operation, wire ABI
or machine check changed.

## D-232 Machine mutations get one bounded second observation after an inconclusive first — Status: Accepted (2026-08-29), advances PW-001

**Context.** The first closing sweep of the 276-entry registry caught 270
mutations through the exact witness each named and found no survivor. Six
entries were inconclusive. One queue mutation no longer compiled after
`PendingTable` encapsulated its slots. The NVMe timeout seam returned through a
self-test-only arm before reaching the production terminal cleanup the
mutation removed. The other four entries reached an unrelated verdict or one
common page fault during the sweep, then reached their exact panic or named
check when rerun unchanged. Treating that incidental first observation as
causal would violate D-209; treating one incidental observation as permanent
would discard a valid, repeatable D-28 witness.

**Decision.** A machine mutation receives exactly one second observation only
when its first observation is inconclusive. An exact catch and a clean survivor
are terminal results and are never sampled until they change. A second
inconclusive observation fails qualification and reports both causes. Build,
boot and observation deadlines remain the existing bounded ones; there is no
open-ended retry.

The forced NVMe timeout now selects a zero-attempt `PollLimit` and falls through
