name exactly that audited trait-member declaration and no concrete self type or
implementation. The route credits the declaration but activates no
implementation body. Indirect supertraits, higher-ranked bounds, aliases,
associated or parameterized `Self` types, and every other ambiguous shape
retain D-275's exact-one rule and fail closed when it cannot be met.

For an explicit qself path call, argument zero is an ordinary argument and
never receiver-type evidence. A full trait path is never reduced to its
terminal name. An exact local type may credit the one selected local default
only when no applicable or unresolved override exists. A compiler-selected
inherent method or free function suppresses unrelated trait routing. An
external trait implementation requires direct implementation evidence or an
exact `Self` together with an explicit trait qualifier; bare method syntax and
a matching member name are insufficient. One `DispatchResolution` value drives
both liveness and refusal reporting so the two consumers cannot disagree.

**Alternatives and proof obligation.** Per-site allowlists and replacing the
type-safe generic APIs with concrete wrappers were rejected because they move
an audit limitation into production design. Activating every candidate was
rejected because it would turn uncertainty into false reachability. Focused
fixtures cover direct and `where` bounds, parameterized direct bounds, the
static-associated-function argument trap, concrete evidence at a generic site,
rejected indirect and non-parameter shapes, a local default beside a sibling
override, inherent/free-function collisions, explicit and untyped external
dispatch, and the earlier ambiguity/specialization refusals. They also drive
the shared resolution through both liveness and failure reporting.

Fifteen independent breaks each made its exact fixture red before restoration:
qself argument zero, declaration-only routing, name-only activation, concrete
Self admission, parameterized and full qualifiers, direct-bound membership,
callee/Self evidence partition, local defaults, ordinary-call exclusion,
external qualifier admission, both shared-resolution consumers, callee
priority and same-terminal trait paths. Those defects remain mutations 1,328
through 1,342. Earlier dispatch and constructor-span mutations whose anchors
moved were re-anchored and re-proven rather than dropped. The complete 123-test
debug API family passes. The release family, real API audit and full current CI
remain required; no result from the failed run is promoted to passing evidence.

## D-292 The orchestrator binary is optimized; the graphs it audits are not — Status: Accepted (2026-09-06), amends D-17 and D-213

**Context.** `cargo xtask` built the orchestrator with the plain `dev`
profile. The API audit hashes a 119 MB materialized registry and parses the
whole workspace with `syn` many times per gate; unoptimized, one audit ran for
more than two and a half hours without finishing, and the ordinary gate could
not complete. Optimizing the `dev` profile for the orchestrator package
instead made every audited test harness and every host-test rebuild in the
mutation sweep carry optimized codegen, which moved the cost rather than
removing it.

**Decision.** `Cargo.toml` declares an `xtask` profile that inherits `dev`
and sets `opt-level = 3`. Only the `cargo xtask` alias selects it. Host tests,
the audited graphs, the mutation workspace and every kernel build keep the
profiles they had, and the tool's own debug assertions and overflow checks
stay on because the profile inherits them. The audit's discovery stage fell
from more than ten minutes to about thirty-five seconds.

**Alternatives.** A per-package `dev` override was measured first and
rejected for the reason above. Building the tool with `--release` was
rejected because that profile enables LTO and would make every tool edit
cost a full relink.

## D-293 Every static lock in `wost` is reclaimed by the panic path, and a contract says so — Status: Accepted (2026-09-06), amends D-41 and D-67

**Context.** `wost::panic::reclaim` force-unlocks the locks a panic may have
interrupted so the reporter can use them. Its comment said that every lock in
a `static` inside the crate belongs in that list and that nothing but the
comment would catch an omission. Three statics had already been omitted: the
paging module's retained-stack ledgers and the PCI configuration lock. The
reporter does not take them today, so no panic deadlocked, but the obligation
was a comment and the comment was false.

**Decision.** Each `wost` module that owns a static `SpinLock` or
`ThreadLock` exposes one `force_unlock(&PanicToken)` that reclaims every such
static, and `panic::reclaim` calls each module's door. A source contract in
`xtask/src/contracts.rs` parses every `wost` source file, collects the static
locks per module, and requires the module door to name each of them and the
panic path to name each module. Adding a static lock without extending the
door, or a door without extending the panic path, fails the host gate.

**Proof.** Two retained mutations delete one module door call and one static
from a door; each reds only the contract. The reclaim order is unchanged and
force-unlock remains sound for the reason `SpinLock::force_unlock` states:
the interrupted holder never resumes.

## D-294 The audited registry is rebound once per compiler round — Status: Accepted (2026-09-06), amends D-263 and D-275

**Context.** The API audit materializes the locked registry into a private
Cargo home and proves it unchanged by hashing every file it holds. D-275's
implementation repeated that proof after every compiler graph: forty-four
graphs per round, nineteen rounds, each proof reading 6,853 files and 119 MB.
The source copy and the original tree are small and stay cheap to rebind, but
the registry proof alone cost more per round than the compilation it guarded.

**Decision.** `compile_graph` still rebinds the copied and original source
trees after every graph, before any diagnostic is read. The registry is
rebound once after the pristine round and once after every instrumented
round, before that round's target libraries are rechecked and before any
verdict is derived. Cargo metadata discovery keeps its own registry proof.

**Why this loses nothing.** Neither placement observes a change made and
reverted inside one compilation; both detect a change that persists to the
next proof. Under either placement no verdict is derived from diagnostics
whose inputs failed a proof, because a failed proof ends the audit. What the
per-round proof changes is the number of graphs whose diagnostics are
discarded together when tampering is found, which is not a property the
verdict depends on.

**Proof.** The retained copied-source and original-source rebind mutations
were re-anchored to the new guard block and still red their exact shape
tests; a new mutation deleting the per-round registry proof reds the shape
test that requires it before the round's target-library recheck.

## D-295 A type-qualified external-trait call is resolved by its callee type's one audited implementation — Status: Accepted (2026-09-06), amends D-291; advances PW-544

**Context.** The first optimized full audit refused thirteen live sites of
the form `Type::from(value)`: `wost::mm::DmaSegment::from`,
`mm::USegment::from` and `EnableFailure::from` in the kernel, its self-tests
and `pci-config`. Each names an exact audited type in its callee path and
calls a `core::convert::From` implementation that the audited crate declares
exactly once for that type. D-291 admitted an external trait implementation
only with an explicit `<Type as Trait>::member` qualifier, because bare method
syntax can auto-reference into a different implementation and a matching
member name alone is not evidence. A static path call has neither weakness:
the compiler resolves `Type::member` against that one type's inherent items
and then the traits implemented for it, and an inherent or free selection is
already visible to the audit and already excludes trait routing.

**Decision.** At a static path call whose callee path names an exact,
non-alias, non-generic audited type and carries no explicit `qself`, an
external-trait activation for that same type is matched exactly as the
explicitly qualified form is; the type's audited implementation inventory
supplies the qualifier. D-275's exact-one rule then decides: one matching
implementation is credited, and two implementations of one generic trait for
one type still fail closed until the call site is written in the qualified
form. Method syntax, explicit `qself` without a trait, aliased callees and
generic callee arguments keep D-291's refusal, and argument zero never
supplies the `Self` of a path call whose callee could not, so an aliased
callee fails closed instead of borrowing its argument's type.

**Why this is exact.** Two different external traits offering one member
name for one type make `Type::member` a compile error, so they cannot reach
the audit. The remaining competitor is a `core` blanket implementation of the
same trait for every type. The reflexive `From` and `TryFrom` conversions
cannot survive the gate because clippy's `useless_conversion` is denied, and
the `Into`, `TryInto`, `ToOwned`, `ToString` and `Borrow` blankets can only
mis-credit a site whose audited crate implements that trait directly beside a
second conversion to the same type, which no audited crate does. The
qualified form of D-291 does not compare trait generic arguments either, so
this route is neither wider nor narrower than it.

**Alternatives.** Rewriting the thirteen sites as `<Type as From<_>>::from`
was rejected because it changes production source to fit an audit
limitation, the reason D-291 itself refused per-site allowlists. Crediting
every candidate was rejected because it turns an ambiguity into false
reachability. Crediting by member name without the callee's type evidence was
rejected because it is the D-291 defect in another form.

**Proof.** Three fixtures cover the admitted call, a two-implementation
refusal that counts both candidates, and an aliased callee that refuses
rather than borrowing argument zero. Two manual breaks each reddened only
their own fixture before restoration and remain mutations 1,352 and 1,353;
the two D-291 mutations whose anchor this decision moved were re-anchored and
re-proven. The real audit and the complete gate on the unchanged tree remain
PW-544's closing evidence.

## D-296 A refused BAR bind returns its reason, and a retained authority keeps no retry accessor — Status: Accepted (2026-09-06), amends D-249 and D-285; closes PW-546

**Context.** The first complete audit after D-291 and D-295, with every
dispatch resolved, reported three public items with no caller:
`BarAuthorityFailure::reason` and `BarAuthorityFailure::into_authority` in
`pci-config`, and `BarBindFailure::into_range` in `wost`. D-285 moved the
kernel to retaining a refused BAR-authority release whole, in its bounded
quarantine, so nothing reads the reason or recovers the authority for a retry
that no pre-Wizzy path makes. A refused bind carried the admitted device
range back to the kernel, which discarded it: `AdmittedDeviceRange` is a
proof this CPU derives from the immutable boot map and its own width, holds
no ledger entry and has no `Drop`, so keeping it buys nothing and dropping it
loses nothing.

**Decision.** `wost::arch::x86_64::pci::bind_memory_bar` returns
`Result<AdmittedBar, BarBindError>`; the `BarBindFailure` wrapper is gone and
the kernel maps the error directly. `BarAuthorityFailure` keeps its private
reason and authority, its `Display` and `Error` implementations, and loses
both accessors. The quarantine still holds the authority, so a future reclaim
path adds its accessor together with its caller, which is the only order the
audit admits.

**Alternatives.** Manufacturing a caller, such as logging the reason at the
quarantine, was rejected because a log line is not a design need and would
hide the next dead accessor behind the same trick. Keeping the range in the
bind refusal under a retained-owner name was rejected because a re-derivable
proof is not an owner, and calling it one would misstate what a refusal can
lose.

**Proof.** The audit that found the three items is the check; its two
retained mutations already prove it can fail. Clippy on every registered
graph, the seventy-two `pci-config` tests and the reviewed-unsafe inventory
pass after the removal, and the complete gate on the unchanged tree closes
PW-546.

## D-297 The population run attests the advisory database; the pinned audit is bound by Git — Status: Accepted (2026-09-06), amends D-274; advances PW-028

**Context.** The first real `cargo xtask qualify-advisory` on a clean commit
failed with "cargo-audit `last-commit` is not a string". D-274 required the
revision-pinned `--no-fetch` report to name the exact database revision.
`cargo-audit` 0.22.2 learns a database commit only from the fetch it
performs: the same tool against the same checkout reports
`"last-commit":"5a0e…"` when it fetches and `"last-commit":null,
"last-updated":null` under `--no-fetch`. Reproduced by hand outside the
qualification, so D-274's pinned-run expectation could never be met by the
tool it names.

**Decision.** The two runs keep their roles and both are recorded. The
population run's report is the tool's attestation: its `last-commit` must
equal the Git revision captured after it and its `last-updated` must be an
RFC3339 time, which the record repeats as `database.last-updated`. The
pinned run's report is the verdict; its database identity may be null, the
shape `--no-fetch` produces, or the exact revision, and it must count the
same advisories the population run saw. The verdict is bound to the revision
by the checkout identity proven identical before and after it, exactly as
D-274 already required. Both transcripts are artifacts of the record and of
the evidence bundle, whose schema becomes v6 because its file set grew.
Offline replay verifies the population transcript as fetched, the pinned
transcript as pinned, their agreement, and the record's repeated time.

**Alternatives.** Dropping `--no-fetch` from the pinned run was rejected
because the verdict would again run against a database the tool may change
while it works, the defect D-274 removed. Accepting a null identity in a
fetched report was rejected because it would discard the one attestation the
tool can make. Keeping only the population run was rejected because the
verdict would then have no run whose inputs were frozen and re-verified
around it.

**Proof.** A unit fixture shows the null identity is accepted only under the
pinned binding; replay fixtures refuse a population transcript without
identity, a pinned audit that saw a different advisory count, and a record
whose repeated update time is malformed or differs from the attested one.
Four manual breaks each reddened only their fixture before restoration and
remain mutations 1,354 through 1,357; the three D-274 report mutations whose
anchors moved into the binding match were re-anchored and re-proven.

## D-298 Git pathname bytes precede filesystem path semantics — Status: Accepted (2026-09-10), amends D-208; closes PW-030

**Context.** The first current clean `cargo xtask mutate` stopped before its
baselines with "Git tracked paths are not unique and sorted". Git returned its
index in strict raw pathname order, but the mutation driver converted each
name to `PathBuf` before comparing it. Component-wise path order disagrees
with Git at a file/directory stem boundary: `boot/limine.conf` correctly
precedes `boot/limine/BOOTX64.EFI` as index bytes but not as path components.
The validation therefore refused the repository it was meant to protect.

**Decision.** The tracked inventory is checked for strict byte order and
uniqueness while it is still the NUL-delimited output Git supplied. Each entry
is then required to be UTF-8 and a confined relative path before conversion to
`PathBuf`. Filesystem paths remain the authority for later containment and
file operations; they no longer redefine the ordering of Git's source
identity.

Sorting after conversion was rejected because it would hide producer disorder
and collapse the distinction between validation and normalization. Removing
the order check was rejected because a duplicate or reordered identity could
then reach digesting and workspace publication.

**Proof.** The real sweep on 05412f8 reproduced the pre-baseline refusal. An
extracted parser test failed under the old component comparison and accepts
the real file/directory boundary under byte comparison; a second test refuses
both duplicate and reversed inventories. Changing the strict comparison from
`<` to `!=` made only the reversed case red before restoration. That defect
remains mutation 1,358; the complete current sweep remains PW-001.

## D-299 Canonical paths stop at the GNU process boundary — Status: Accepted (2026-09-10), amends D-208; closes PW-031

**Context.** The next clean mutation attempt reached its pristine host
baseline, where every Rust build failed in MinGW's linker. The isolated
workspace correctly supplied its canonical Windows target path, whose
`\\?\` verbatim prefix preserves filesystem identity. Cargo passed that path
through to the GNU linker, which parsed the prefix as a root-relative path and
reported every generated object as missing. Repeating from the thirteen-byte
checkout root `C:\wq55a30dd` produced the same failure, ruling out path length.

**Decision.** Filesystem validation, containment, copying, journaling and
artifact lookup retain canonical paths. The API auditor's existing
child-process path adapter moves into the shared Cargo driver, is narrowed to
verbatim disk and UNC paths, and becomes the one boundary used by ordinary
builds, contract probes, mutation host tests and the audit itself. Other
Windows prefixes and every non-Windows path pass through unchanged. The
private target remains the same directory and the path loses no absolute
component; only syntax the GNU tools cannot consume is removed.

Weakening canonicalization throughout the mutation workspace was rejected
because subprocess compatibility cannot choose source or state identity.
Depending on a shorter checkout was rejected by the short-root reproduction.
A relative target was rejected because its meaning would then depend on each
subprocess working directory instead of the already-confined build authority.

**Proof.** A command-construction test failed with the verbatim disk path under
the old boundary and passes with its ordinary equivalent. A second test does
the same for a verbatim UNC path. The moved disk-path defect remains the
existing mutation 1,048; replacing the UNC conversion arm with pass-through
behavior reddened its exact test before restoration and remains mutation
1,359. The complete current sweep remains PW-001.

## D-300 Qualification fixtures own their source-control premise — Status: Accepted (2026-09-10), amends D-208; closes PW-032

**Context.** The clean mutation sweep on 1ddef80 passed the repaired linker
boundary, then its pristine host baseline failed in
`streamed_model_tree_digest_preserves_the_length_delimited_schema`. That test
used its compile-time repository path and asked Git for the real `models/`
inventory. D-208 deliberately runs tests from a tracked-file copy with no
`.git`; the test therefore required authority the isolated source does not
contain, even though its subject was only equivalence between streamed and
legacy digest encodings.

**Decision.** The compatibility test creates a uniquely named temporary Git
repository, writes two differently named and sized model inputs, stages them,
and compares the production streamed digest with its independent in-memory
encoding there. Production model qualification still discovers the real
tracked tree from the clean repository and retains every source-bound check.

Skipping the test outside a Git checkout was rejected because the mutation
baseline would then prove less than ordinary CI. Copying `.git` into D-208's
workspace was rejected because mutable source-control state is not a build
input and would weaken isolation. Continuing to borrow the live repository was
rejected because a unit fixture must own every premise needed to reproduce its
claim.

**Proof.** The real isolated host baseline failed with "no tracked model inputs
were found" while ordinary CI passed. The private two-file repository passes
from the ordinary checkout. Replacing the streamed path-length frame with zero
reddened its exact digest comparison before restoration; the existing defect
remains mutation 877. The complete current sweep remains PW-001.

## D-301 A complete mutation report is a repair inventory, not a production verdict — Status: Accepted (2026-09-11), amends D-119 and D-244; advances PW-001

**Context.** The first clean complete run of the 1,359-entry current registry
finished on `f28428a`: 1,301 mutations were caught, 34 survived and 24 were
inconclusive. The report is source-, registry- and index-bound and therefore
settles which attempts ran. It does not settle that every survivor identifies
a missing production invariant. Mutation 344 changed the active-table choice
for mirrored FAT32 volumes, but the preceding parser guard already requires
their selector to be zero, so the changed branch could not alter behavior.
Mutation 567 changed the pairwise half-open overlap helper, but named a test
that exercises only the bitmap path; an existing reversed-adjacency assertion
does exercise the helper and failed under the defect.

**Decision.** PW-001 uses the complete report as its exact repair inventory.
A survivor is closed by strengthening a real proof gap or by replacing a
non-load-bearing mutation with a defect that removes the stated invariant. An
inconclusive attempt is repaired until it compiles and reaches its named
witness; a different failure is not credited. A mutation may name only a check
that executes its changed path. Redundant guards are not weakened merely to
make a partial mutation observable: their mutation must remove the complete
property or target one independently observable layer.

The FAT32 entry now removes the parser's rejection of a nonzero selector while
mirroring is active and names the existing meaningless-selector test. The port
entry keeps its original half-open defect and names the existing pairwise
reservation test. The other 56 reported outcomes remain open inventory, not
silently adjudicated equivalents.

**Proof.** With the port overlap changed from `<` to `<=`, only
`tests::a_request_that_overlaps_itself_is_refused` failed at the reversed
adjacent spans. With the mirrored-selector guard replaced by `false`, only
`tests::extended_flags_reject_reserved_bits_and_meaningless_selectors` failed
at flags `0x0001`. Both production changes were restored before the registry
edits. The ordinary gate proves that each replacement still matches once; the
next clean complete sweep remains PW-001's closing evidence.

## D-302 Redundant path defenses need layer-specific witnesses — Status: Accepted (2026-09-12), amends D-263 and D-301; advances PW-001

**Context.** Complete-sweep mutations 886 and 887 each survived the same SPDX
symlink fixture. That fixture installed the redirect before the read began, so
either the pre-open direct-file check or the post-read revalidation could
reject it. The two checks are deliberately redundant against that static
input, but they own different moments: the first prevents following a redirect
at open, while the second detects pathname substitution after the checked
handle exists. One test could not prove either layer independently.

**Decision.** Retain both defenses and give each an observer that reaches only
its layer. The pre-open fixture installs a redirect first and uses the existing
post-measurement hook to prove the file was never opened. The post-read fixture
opens a direct file, replaces its pathname with a symlink through that hook,
proves the substitution completed and requires the final identity check to
refuse it. Each mutation names only its layer-specific test.

**Proof.** Removing the pre-open check made
`supply_chain_text_rejects_a_redirect_before_opening` fail because its hook ran.
After restoration, removing the final check made
`supply_chain_text_revalidates_its_path_after_reading` fail because the read
returned successfully after the fixture substituted the pathname. Both exact
tests pass with the defenses restored, and the registry source and check-name
proofs pass. The remaining complete-report outcomes and a clean successor
sweep stay in PW-001.

## D-303 Redundant capture bounds need phase-specific witnesses — Status: Accepted (2026-09-12), amends D-264 and D-301; advances PW-001

**Context.** Complete-sweep mutations 870 and 871 replaced the caller's child
output limit with the global ceiling during polling and final collection. Both
survived one integrated fixture: while either correct check remained, it
rejected the same 4 KiB output against the 32-byte caller limit. D-264 requires
both phases because a live child must be stopped before it fills the capture,
and a child observed exiting still must not allocate beyond its caller's bound.

**Decision.** Keep the shared limit at both phases and make their observations
independent. The noisy child now flushes its output and remains live, so its
test requires the polling observer to report the 32-byte overflow rather than
eventually report a timeout. Final collection is routed through a small private
helper used by the production call and its retained-handle fixture, so that
fixture reaches collection without a live polling phase.

**Proof.** Substituting the global limit in the polling closure made
`a_caller_specific_capture_limit_is_polled_while_the_child_is_live` wait to its
two-second deadline and fail its overflow assertion. After restoration,
substituting the global limit in the collection helper made
`captured_output_cannot_grow_collection_memory_past_its_limit` accept six bytes
against a five-byte limit. Both exact tests pass after restoration, and the
registry source and check-name proofs pass. The remaining complete-report
outcomes and a clean successor sweep stay in PW-001.

## D-304 Qualification parser invariants need pre-record witnesses — Status: Accepted (2026-09-12), amends D-274, D-297 and D-301; advances PW-001

**Context.** Complete-sweep mutation 26 removed the nonempty advisory-database
check but survived the integrated forged-report test. That fixture changed its
transcript from one advisory to zero while its already-authored qualification
record still claimed one, so the later record comparison rejected the mismatch
even when the semantic parser accepted the empty database. The test proved the
whole verifier failed, but not that an empty population result could never
author a matching record.

**Decision.** Keep the integrated hostile-report matrix and add one direct
semantic-report witness before record binding. It supplies an otherwise valid,
revision-bound fetched report with an advisory count of zero and requires the
specific empty-database refusal. The retained mutation names that exact test.

**Proof.** With the nonempty guard replaced by the registry defect,
`an_empty_advisory_database_cannot_author_a_qualification` failed because
`verify_advisory_report` returned `AdvisoryFacts` with a zero count. After
restoration, the exact test and the registry source/check-name proofs pass. The
remaining complete-report outcomes and a clean successor sweep stay in PW-001.

## D-305 Parent-substitution witnesses isolate the claimed verification layer — Status: Accepted (2026-09-12), amends D-244, D-301 and D-302; advances PW-001

**Context.** Complete-sweep mutations 42 and 44 removed the parent checks from
outer evidence-bundle and qualification-snapshot verification, yet their named
tests survived. Each fixture copied only `model/record` into its alternate
directory before linking that directory over the accepted `model` parent. Even
without the mutated check, iteration failed at the next absent model transcript.
The assertions therefore credited an unrelated incomplete-fixture error instead
of observing whether identical accepted bytes could arrive through a linked
parent. After preserving the complete tree, mutation 42 still remained masked:
the bounded hashing layer deliberately repeats its own real-parent check before
opening the file.

**Decision.** A parent-authority witness changes only parent authority, and a
redundant layer gets its own observation. The snapshot fixture renames the
complete accepted model directory to an adjacent real directory and links its
original pathname back to that same directory. Every file, byte and filesystem
object remains present. The evidence fixture selects the registered model
record, installs the same linked parent and observes immediately after the outer
bundle-path check but before hashing begins. The production path and hashing
checks remain independent and unchanged.

Copying the full directory entry by entry was rejected because it adds fixture
machinery and can accidentally omit a future registered artifact. Keeping the
partial fixture was rejected because any missing file could satisfy the broad
error assertion before the mutated path was observed. Removing the hashing
layer's repeated validation was rejected because a boundary proof must not
weaken the defense it is meant to test.

**Proof.** Removing `checked_bundle_file` from qualification digesting made the
pre-hash observer run and failed
`a_bundle_parent_link_is_rejected_before_qualification_hashing`; the hashing
layer still refused the link afterward. After restoration, removing the
snapshot's contained-file check made
`a_snapshot_parent_link_cannot_substitute_qualification_bytes` accept the
complete linked tree. Each exact test passes with its guard restored; the
registry source and check-name proofs pass. The remaining complete-report
outcomes and a clean successor sweep stay in PW-001.
